basis: US dollars per million tokens, on the four disjoint counts of a usage record: input (neither read from nor written to a cache), cache_read, cache_write and output. A fifth count, cache_write_1h_tokens, is not disjoint: it is part of cache_write_tokens. A harness that reports input including the cached part has to subtract it before the record is written (the Codex adapter does). A model is listed under every id a harness may report it by (claude-haiku-4-5 and its dated id are separate entries with the same prices). cache_write is the 5-minute write price; a harness that charges nothing extra for cache writes (OpenAI gpt-5) has it equal to input. cache_write_1h, where a model has one (Claude), is the price of a write at the 1-hour rate: Claude Code bills its writes there, and the part of cache_write_tokens written at that rate is cache_write_1h_tokens, priced at cache_write_1h instead of cache_write. gpt-6.1-sol is the short-context standard rate (up to 272K input tokens); its cache write is the 30-minute write price, and the long-context rate is not modelled, so a run above 272K input tokens is under-estimated.
